title: Card orchestration, token-scaling and gesture prototype for compact cost canvases
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Deliver a compact, adaptive card choreography and token scaling approach for the Cost Explorer canvas that preserves legibility, reduces visual noise at high density, and enables smooth rollout states (canary / baseline / degraded) across consoles.

Scope:
- Define a responsive token scaling system (typography, spacing, elevation) that maps to three density tiers (compact, default, spacious) and a high-density ‘inspect’ mode.
- Prototype an orchestration system for metric cards that supports reflow, prioritized reveal, and gesture-driven focus (tap / long-press / two-finger drag) for touch and trackpad users.
- Produce a Figma library with component variants, token names and usage guidelines, plus exportable specs for engineering to consume runtime flags for density and rollout states.
- Accessibility: color contrast passes for all density modes, focus order and screen reader labels for interactive gestures, and reduced-motion variants.

Deliverables:
- Figma prototype file (library + three interactive canvases): density switching, gesture focus, rollout overlays.
- Design spec doc with token mapping to runtime keys, expected breakpoints, and acceptance criteria.
- Small QA checklist for visual regressions and accessibility tests.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Compact card variant displays 20% more items per row without truncating key labels at typical viewport widths.
2) Token scaling rules are implemented in Figma tokens and annotated with runtime flag names (e.g., console.density=compact).
3) Gesture interactions are documented with clear fallbacks for non-touch devices and keyboard equivalents.
4) Contrast ratios >= 4.5:1 for body text across all tokens; examples included in spec.
5) Engineering sign-off on token mapping and exportable CSS/JSON naming convention.

Constraints & Decisions so far:
- We will keep numerical spacing tokens (space-2/4/8) but introduce density multipliers rather than duplicating tokens. This minimizes token explosion.
- For gestures, we restrict primary focus affordance to one gesture (long-press) and provide a keyboard shortcut to avoid ambiguous multi-gesture mapping.
- Rollout overlays will be lightweight banners rather than modal dialogs to avoid disrupting analytics flows.

Links and artifacts:
- Figma prototype: https://www.figma.com/file/REDACTED/compact-card-choreo (internal)
- PRD (drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/REDACTED
- Engineering ticket for runtime flags: ENG-40211

Notes for implementation handoff:
- Provide token-to-runtime mapping table with exact key names and recommended default values.
- Supply two visual regression test frames per density mode for CI snapshots.
- Include a short demo clip (10-15s) showing gesture focus and card reveal for product review.
